Census blocks with place assignments and Hispanic or Latino counts

Source: R/seg_blocks.R
seg_blocks.Rd

Downloads decennial census block counts of the total and Hispanic or Latino population for a state, assigns each block to its place with the Census Bureau's Block Assignment File, and optionally attaches block polygons.

Usage

seg_blocks(
  state,
  year,
  universe = c("total", "vap"),
  county = NULL,
  geometry = TRUE
)

Arguments

state

State postal abbreviation, name, or two-digit FIPS code, such as "CA".

year

Decennial census year, 2010 or 2020.

universe

"total" for the whole population or "vap" for the voting-age population (18 and over). For voting rights work use "vap": courts look at citizen voting-age population (CVAP), which is not published for blocks, so VAP is the closest block-level count.

county

Optional county names or three-digit FIPS codes to limit the download. NULL (the default) returns every county in the state, as listed in the Block Assignment File for that census year.

geometry

If TRUE (the default), return an sf object with TIGER/Line block polygons.

Value

An sf object (a tibble when geometry = FALSE) with one row per block and columns block_geoid, place_geoid (state plus place FIPS code), year, universe, total, and latino.

Details

Counts come from tidycensus::get_decennial(), one county at a time, so a Census API key is needed (see tidycensus::census_api_key()). The 2010 counts are from Summary File 1 and the 2020 counts from the PL 94-171 redistricting file:

YearUniversetotallatino
2010totalP004001P004003
2010vapP011001P011002
2020totalP2_001NP2_002N
2020vapP4_001NP4_002N

Places are incorporated places and census designated places. Each block is assigned whole, using the INCPLACE_CDP table of the Block Assignment File for the same census, rather than by overlaying geometries. Blocks outside every place get NA in place_geoid.

The Census Bureau added noise to 2020 block counts to protect confidentiality, so they are more reliable summed over many blocks than read one block at a time.

Polygons come from tigris::blocks(). Set options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE) to keep them between sessions. The 2020 block shapefile is published only for whole states (382 MB zipped for California), so county shortens the polygon download only for 2010.

See also

seg_measures() and seg_clusters(), which take this output.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
san_benito <- seg_blocks("CA", 2020, county = "San Benito")
seg_measures(san_benito, by = place_geoid, group = latino, total = total)
}
